1. Move `open/m-<tid>.md` and its bodies, `open/m-<tid>-*.md`, to `closed/`.

## What is not here

- No inbox file. What is pending for a member is a query over `open/`, so a lost or stale inbox
  cannot disagree with the threads.
- No counter file per thread. The next number is read from the thread itself.
- No format version in the lines. The README's version is the rules', fields are additive,
  and a reader takes what is there.
- No second machine. The thread ids and line numbers are allocated under one clone's mutex, so
  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times
  are UTC to the second. The migration restored `m-1` from history without its blank line, its
  surplus `done` marks still valid lines.
- v0.3.0, the cutover from v0.2.0's records and inboxes: every record was complete, so no
  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

# Todo list

This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

The other files:

- [BUGS.md](BUGS.md): List of vc-x1 bugs that should be addressed 
- [zDOING.md](zDOING.md): the cycle being worked on, its planning and its work's documentation,
  and the continuation notes a session leaves for the next.
- [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md): the last finished cycle's record, kept until the next one closes.
- [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md): the bugs.

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

- **Retire the frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md`.** (wink, 2026-08-27) They
  are frozen and no longer grow, and the agent-repo transcript plus git history hold what they
  hold. Delete both in one cycle, after a sweep turns every link into them (Todo entries, the
  backlog, rationale.md, the other members' messages) into a permalink at the SHA before the
  deletion.
  - Waits on: **`vc-x1 closed "<title>"`** landed, and the session viewer good enough to read
    a cycle's record from the transcript.
  - Place when unblocked: first.
- **Sync's remote look stops spawning git.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-09) Sync learns where a
  remote's bookmarks are by spawning `git ls-remote`, and downloads the commits of the ones that
  moved by spawning a `git fetch` that moves no ref, the sixth entry of the spawn register in
  `clippy.toml` and the one spawn of `git`. Replace `git_command` and its two callers in
  `src/jj/session.rs` with jj-lib's query, delete the `#[allow]`, and close the entry.
  - Waits on: jj-lib's public API offering that query. Neither 0.45.1 nor 0.46.0 has one:
    `rg -i 'ls.remote' src/` in the jj-lib source prints nothing, and its git subprocess layer is
    `pub(crate)`. An upstream feature request, once filed or found, is named here.
  - Place when unblocked: first, being one function.

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) A project's `custom.md` holds what is true of one machine, the family's
paths and the session's standing permissions, so committing it makes every clone assume a
development environment that exists only here. The family is local: no repo assumes one, and the
layer a member shares with its family lives with the family, not in the member's repo.

- `custom.md` is gitignored and untracked, and the agent reads it when there is one: the rule
  **Read custom.md first**, [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)'s first step, and
  [custom.md](AGENTS.md#custommd) say so, and the last says it is local.
- A project convention that must be committed goes into the agent-file it belongs to, its diff
  from the payload the proposal, as [Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)
  already allows.
- Open: whether the payload ships no `custom.md` or an example under another name.
- An `agent-files` proposal, its own cycle, ahead of the code entries below, which follow from it.

Agreed. Making the untracking the cycle's goal is a better shape than the one in `zCLOSED.md` now. Here's how I'd reshape it.

**Why it fits now**
- The commit hasn't been pushed and has no bookmark, so the cycle record can be rewritten freely.
- The `.gitignore` change already in the working copy is the actual change. The five Todo entries are its documentation and the follow-on plan, which is what a single-step cycle carries in one commit.
- It's convention work, so it can't be bundled into a feature cycle. It doesn't need to be: this cycle becomes the convention cycle.

**How `zCLOSED.md` would change**
- **Title**: something like `chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored`. The current title describes only the Todo entries, which become the smaller part.
- **Problem**: this is a public repo meant for anyone to clone, and they won't be family members. A committed `custom.md` gives every clone a layer for one machine: the family's sibling paths and your standing permissions.
- **Deliberation**: keep what's there (the family is local, the abandoned family-directory bookmark, fixtures named by their source) and add:
  - Untracking comes first. Fixing the agent-files wording comes in a later proposal cycle.
  - The file stays on disk here and is gone from the tree from this commit on. Older commits still hold it, and it contains nothing sensitive.
- **Solution**: `custom.md` is untracked and in `.gitignore`, and the five entries open `## Todo`. The first entry shrinks: its "gitignored and untracked" bullet is now done, so what remains is the `AGENTS.md` wording ("read it when there is one") and the open question of whether the template ships an example file.
- **Acceptance check**:
  - `git ls-files custom.md` prints nothing after the commit, and `custom.md` is still on disk.
  - `vc-x1 validate` passes.
  - The real test of "anyone can clone it": clone it fresh into `tmp/` and run `cargo build` and `cargo test` there. I'm not sure whether `vc-x1 validate-anchors` follows `AGENTS.md`'s links to `custom.md`. If it does, it would fail in a fresh clone, and the check would show that.

**Caveats to state honestly in the record**
- **"Just works" holds for building and testing, not yet for the agent.**
  - `AGENTS.md` still says "Read custom.md first" with no "if there is one", so an agent in a fresh clone gets an instruction it can't follow. That's what Todo entry 1 fixes.
  - `.vc-config.md`'s `[family]` and `[test] fixtures` still name paths that exist only on this machine. In a clone, the fixture tests skip silently and pass, which is the "missing fixture" entry.
  - None of these block a clone, but the record shouldn't claim more than the commit does.
- **Other clones lose their copy.** Any existing clone of this repo on another machine would have its `custom.md` deleted when it pulls this commit, because removing a tracked file deletes it from the checkout. Probably no such clone exists, but if one does, back up its `custom.md` first.

**Process**: before the commit, sync and create a bookmark named after the new title. Then validate, review, and push.

content.content:
### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)

([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))

A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The two surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)`: the title
  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).

The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.
...
A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope
slot then carries what the declaration says rather than a component. A project's own declarations
live in its `custom.md`, and the set declares for itself:

- `agent-files`, the set's own lifecycle: `agent-files(<scope>): vX.Y.Z`, the description being the
  agent-files version in its `v` spelling ([Agent-files
  version](versioning.md#agent-files-version)), which keeps the formulaic titles unique and is the
  one version a title may carry ([Versions live in the version-of-record
  only](#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)).
  - The two scopes:
    - `proposal`, outbound work for others to adopt. The cycle bumps the agent-files version, and
      the title names the new one.
    - `adoption`, inbound. The cycle copies the source's version file, and the title names what it
      took.
  - Who proposed to whom, or adopted from whom, is the message record's `from:` and `to:`, never
    the title's.
  - `git log --grep 'agent-files('` finds every agent-files title, the recurring type being the
    token that collects the thread.

### Steps are named, not numbered

A step has a title and no number. Nothing in a ladder rung or a commit gives a step an ordinal: a
rung's place in the list already *is* its place in the ladder, so a number beside it would restate
the position and then have to be maintained.

- **The title is the identifier.** A record points at a step by its title, a plain greppable
  mention, which is why the title is verbatim-identical across the three surfaces.
- **Unambiguous, not globally unique.** Two titles must be distinguishable where a title is
...
[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).

- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
  that introduced it.
- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **An adoption is a copy and a check**: `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c <src>` takes the set and the
  family's `custom.md` with it, and `vc-x1 agent-files diff -c <src>` is the adoption's last act,
  exiting zero when the two copies are the same. An adopter that keeps a `custom.md` of its own
  drops the `-c` from both, which is its prerogative.
- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) This is a public repo, meant to be cloned by anyone, and they will not
be members of the vc-x1 family. A committed `custom.md` hands every clone one machine's layer: the
family's sibling paths and the session's standing permissions. The paths in `.vc-config.md`'s
`[family]` and `[test] fixtures` assume the same machine, and a rename of `../vc-x1-fixtures`
showed the cost: `cargo test` still passed, the fixture tests skipping silently. The cycle **feat:
the family directory**, waiting to land, moved the family further into the repo.

#### Deliberation

- The family is local, and no repo assumes one, wink's call. `custom.md` stops being committed,
  and the family's shared layer lives in `../vc-x1-family`.
  - A gitignored `.vc-config.local.md` for the family's paths was weighed and dropped: with the
    shared `custom.md` the agent has the paths, and the tool needs none.
- The untracking comes first, on its own, and the agent-files' wording follows in an
  `agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0` cycle, so the Todo entry that held both was split (2026-10-18).
- `custom.md` stays on disk here and leaves the tree from this commit on. Earlier commits keep it,
  holding nothing private. A clone that pulls this commit has its `custom.md` deleted, and we
  think this machine holds the only one.
- The bookmark of **feat: the family directory** was abandoned unlanded, at wink's go, its six
  commits abandoned and the bookmark deleted locally and on the remote. Its agent-repo commits
  stay, being on the agent-repo's `main` already.
- Fixtures are named by their source, not by a local path: `dr-1` is reproducible and published,
  so its source is the portable fact.
  - Marking the fixture tests `#[ignore]` and running them in `[validate] full` fixes the silent
    pass on its own, so it is its own entry, ranked ahead.
- `init` and `clone` take `--custom`, and `update` waits, since a copied pointer rarely drifts.
- The entries go at the top of `## Todo`, the agent-files proposal first, since the code entries
  follow from it. The ranking is wink's to change.
- Single-step: the untracking, and the five Todo entries that carry the rest.

#### Solution

`custom.md` is gitignored and untracked. Five entries open `## Todo`: the agent-files drop the
family and custom.md is optional, the family leaves the committed config, init and clone take
--custom, a missing fixture fails instead of passing, and fixtures are named by their source.

What a fresh clone gets is a repo that builds and tests. The agent-files still assume a
`custom.md` until the proposal cycle, and the committed config still names this machine's sibling
paths until the family and fixture entries land.

#### Acceptance check

- `jj file list custom.md` prints nothing, and `custom.md` is still on disk.
- `TODO.md > ## Todo` opens with the five entries in that order, and `vc-x1 validate-anchors
  TODO.md zCLOSED.md` passes.
- A fresh clone of the bookmark's commit builds, and its `cargo test` passes.
- Result:

#### Ladder

- chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored (current)

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) This is a public repo, meant to be cloned by anyone, and they will not

content.text:
A clone test that installs is the right proof that "anyone can clone this". It checks that the committed tree builds and installs with its own `Cargo.lock`, without `custom.md` and without this machine's working copy. Two things need settling first.

**1. What gets cloned.** The commit doesn't exist yet. The work is still uncommitted in `@`, and the bookmark points at `main`, so cloning the remote now would test the old tree. Three options:
- **Clone the local repo (my pick).** Put a temporary local bookmark on `@`, never pushed (`jj bookmark set ... -r @`), and clone this directory from `tmp/`:
  - `jj git clone`, then check out that bookmark.
  - `vc-x1 clone ./...`. Its source accepts a local path (`src/clone.rs:1`). It also tries to clone the agent-repo, and I'm not sure what it derives for that from a local path. If it trips there, that's a finding in itself.
  - Delete the temporary bookmark afterwards.
- **Test after the push.** This is the most real test, cloning from GitHub, but the result then lands after the commit. Recording it would be a late tweak to a pushed commit, which needs your approval like any push.
- **Do both.** Local before the push, and a remote check at Land as confirmation.

**2. The `vc-x1-test` rename and `--locked`.** Renaming the package in the clone's `Cargo.toml` makes `cargo install --locked` fail, because the lockfile's root entry still says `vc-x1`. Fixing the lockfile first would defeat the point of `--locked`, which is to prove the committed lock is consistent. Two ways around it:
- **Install the unmodified clone into a scratch directory (my pick):** `cargo install --path . --locked --root tmp/<clone>-install`. The binary is still called `vc-x1`, but it lands in `tmp/`, so `~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1` is never touched. This tests exactly what a stranger would get.
- **If you want the name `vc-x1-test` on your PATH:** do the same `--root` install and copy the binary as `vc-x1-test` (`--root` itself is still needed to keep `~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1` safe). Renaming the package itself is the dev-name mechanism the cycle protocol uses, which does regenerate the lock, and that's a different test.

**Smaller points**
- Run `cargo install` only after checking `custom.md` is absent from each clone, so the record can say the build didn't depend on it. I believe the build doesn't read it: only `src/agent_files/` mentions it, and only at run time.
- Add `cargo test` to the same two clones. Then the `jj git clone` case shows the jj side passes, and a plain `git clone` would reproduce the new `cli_smoke` Todo entry. I'd leave the plain-git case out of this cycle's checks, as you said.

content.text:
`vc-x1 clone` doesn't take a branch. `src/clone.rs` always clones the default branch and then requires `main` to be tracked (`verify_tracking(target_dir, "main")`). There's no `-b`/`--bookmark` option, and the target can't carry a branch name.

It doesn't need one, though. A clone fetches every remote bookmark, so after the push the cycle's bookmark is already in the clone as `chore-custommd-is-untracked-and-gitignored@origin`. The test becomes:

1. `vc-x1 clone https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1 vc-clone` in `tmp/acc`. This clones `main` plus the agent-repo; I'll take the URL from `origin` when we run it.
2. `jj new chore-custommd-is-untracked-and-gitignored@origin` in the clone.
3. Check there's no `custom.md`, then `cargo install --path . --locked --root ../vc-install`.

A `--bookmark <name>` option for `vc-x1 clone`, which would check out the bookmark and track it, is a nice-to-have for a Todo entry, not a blocker.

**When to run it.** A single-step cycle's record is finished inside its one commit, so a check that needs the pushed commit can't put its result there. Two choices:
- **After the push, before Land (my pick).** Run the three steps against the bookmark. A pass is reported to you. A failure is a finding: it gets a Todo entry, and it's your call whether it holds up Land. The record says this check runs after the push and is reported, not recorded.
- **At Land, after `main` is fast-forwarded.** A plain `vc-x1 clone` then gets this commit with no `jj new` step. But by then the commit is already permanent, so a failure can only become a Todo entry.

**Recording the checks**
- The `jj git clone` result can go in the record now as a pass: no `custom.md`, and the `--root` install gave `vc-x1 0.85.2 (agent-files v0.2.9)`, as you saw.
- `vc-x1 clone` of a local jj workspace fails because the source's git `HEAD` is detached, so the clone has no tracked `main`. That's a real bug, since the help lists local paths as sources. It gets a Todo entry, along with the `--bookmark` idea.

**Cleanup before the commit**
- Delete the local `acceptance-local` bookmark. It was never pushed, but a stray local bookmark would confuse a later look.
- Remove `tmp/acc` after your review. It's gitignored, but it holds two builds.

The plain version: `vc-x1 clone` has no branch option, but every clone already contains the bookmark, so after the push you clone, run `jj new <bookmark>@origin`, and install. Record the jj-clone pass now, run the `vc-x1 clone` test after the push and report it, and file the local-path bug and a `--bookmark` option in `TODO.md`.

136:### Commit-body form
137-
138-The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
139-shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
140-problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
141-bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
142-statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.
143-
144-- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
145-  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
146-  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
147-  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
148-  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
149-- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
150-  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
151-  to be more than one commit.
152-- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
153-  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
154-  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
155-- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
156-  form, the general form at its smallest.
157-- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
158-  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
159-  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.
160-
161-**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
162-pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
163-typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
164-read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
165-flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
166-a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.
====
# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) This is a public repo, meant to be cloned by anyone, and they will not
be members of the vc-x1 family. A committed `custom.md` hands every clone one machine's layer: the
family's sibling paths and the session's standing permissions.

#### Deliberation

- The family is local, and no repo assumes one, wink's call. `custom.md` stops being committed,
  and the family's shared layer lives in `../vc-x1-family`.
- This cycle untracks `custom.md` and nothing else, and what follows from it is in `TODO.md`, the
  Todo entry that held the untracking and the agent-files' wording split in two (2026-10-18).
- `custom.md` stays on disk here and leaves the tree from this commit on. Earlier commits keep it,
  holding nothing private. A clone that pulls this commit has its `custom.md` deleted, and we
  think this machine holds the only one.
- A copy of the tree without `custom.md` passed `cargo test` once made a jj repo, and failed three
  `cli_smoke` tests as a plain git repo, a finding older than this cycle, filed as [The CLI smoke
  tests need no jj repo](TODO.md#the-cli-smoke-tests-need-no-jj-repo).

#### Solution

`custom.md` is gitignored and untracked, and the work that follows from it is in `TODO.md > ##
Todo`.

#### Acceptance check

- `jj file list custom.md` prints nothing, `.gitignore` holds `/custom.md`, and `custom.md` is
  still on disk.
- `vc-x1 validate-anchors TODO.md zCLOSED.md` passes.
- A `jj git clone` of the commit's tree holds no `custom.md`, and `cargo install --path . --locked
  --root <scratch>` there installs a `vc-x1` that runs, `~/.cargo/bin` untouched.
- After the push and before Land, a `vc-x1 clone` of the remote, on the bookmark by `jj new
  <bookmark>@origin`, holds no `custom.md` and installs the same way. Its result is reported, not
  recorded, since the commit carrying this record is the one it checks.
- Result: pass. `jj file list custom.md` prints nothing, `.gitignore` holds `/custom.md`, and the
  file is on disk. The anchors check clean. The `jj git clone`, of this repo at a local bookmark
  on the working copy, held no `custom.md` and installed `vc-x1 0.85.2 (agent-files v0.2.9)`.
  - `vc-x1 clone` of the same local path failed, the source's git `HEAD` being detached, so the
    clone tracks no `main`. Filed as [vc-x1 clone of a local jj workspace tracks no
    main](TODO.md#vc-x1-clone-of-a-local-jj-workspace-tracks-no-main), and the remote clone
    after the push stands in for it.

- chore: custom.md is untracked and gitignored (current)

  - push-work        publish <bookmark> to origin
  - squash-push-bot  fold `.claude`'s trailing writes
                     into its commit and push main
